utterances.text: If we could pass along to the next photograph, and again, Mr. Malovic, if you could just indicate to stop at any point if there's further information that you would wish to provide on particular photographs that you're going to be shown.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: This is a photograph of an inmate who had just been released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, one sees on this body spots that one cannot easily identify. Can you comment on those? There's one on the right breast and on the lower arms, on the insides.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say anything with 100 per cent certainty. All I know is that people who came out in this condition said that while they had been imprisoned had been mistreated, beaten up, and abused. Whether what we see on the photograph is a result of such acts I can't say, but we see that these people were starved.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we can pass along to the next photograph, and in fact keep passing through them unless I or the witness intervene, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may just note. If we enlarge this photograph we had just seen, photograph number 2, it would be clear that it was a tattoo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I get that photograph back on the screen? It may be a tattoo on the right side of his chest, but I don't think that what we see on his right lower arm is a tattoo. I'm not sure though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait. We have another question by a Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your written statement you mention two persons who died as a result of their physical conditions. Did they die while you were on the spot? Did you also make photographs of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I mentioned that in my statement; however, that did not happen that day or there. But I heard that one of the prisoners who had been released was in such a poor condition that he simply did not survive. He succumbed a few days later. But I did not see it, and I did not photograph it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one clarification. On several of the photos we see prisoners who were naked from the waist up. Were they naked from the waist up because they were trying to display their physical condition, or was it simply so hot that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It was not extremely hot that day. It was morning, and on some photographs we can see that some other people were dressed a little more warmly. It is simply that I asked my subjects to take off their clothes so that their condition would be more obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person, I see that on -- that his T-shirt is in his hand. So you asked him to take off the T-shirt to photograph him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we move to page 10 of this exhibit, please. Now to page 13 of the same exhibit. Page 28. Page --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, if I may say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please give us your comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see a soldier of the Spanish Battalion of the UNPROFOR helping civilians to get off the truck. The photograph was taken on that same day, on the 28th of August, on the same location which was the hydro power plant of Grabovica, again in the a.m., but it was taken in the tunnel that is right next to the dam. So it looks like a night photograph. And in the background we see a sign -- the sign of the United Nations on the tarpaulin of the truck. We also see a woman who is holding two bags in her left hand, and there I must stress that a large number of refugees came with very few possessions or without any possessions at all, and I remember being told that they were allowed to carry only one or two bags, to pick up just the barest necessities and get ready to travel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see also two young children in this photograph, between 3 and 5 years old, also naked from the waist up, but in this case it wasn't you who asked them to take off their clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, in this case I did not ask them. But it may be that this truck arrived around 11.00, and you see that it is a covered truck, and you can imagine in the beginning of the summer what it was like to travel inside the truck. They must have been hot, feeling hot and that's why they undressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Moving now to page 33. Page 38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Just a minute. On page 33, the person in white, do you know who he is? Because he's apparently not an inmate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who he is. I don't recognise him. But you have to know that in those prisons, before prisoners were released there were people who had spent there a month or two, and there were others who had been brought just two days prior. So there were people who -- whose condition was less poor than that of others.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Next photograph, page 38, please.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph we see a baby carried by her mother out of an UNPROFOR APC. The photograph was taken the same day, the same location.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Moving now to page 44.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: I really have to say something about this one. This one was not taken on the 28th of August; it was taken a couple of months later. I can't tell you the exact time. We see that these refugees, whose story was similar to the story of the refugees that I photographed on the 28th of August, were brought by trucks of the International Red Cross. I can't remember exactly where, but I know that they were brought to Jablanica and that these people got off the truck in the town of Jablanica itself. I think there are a couple of other photographs in the same group taken on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Moving to page 45.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: This is one of the others. So this one was not taken on the 28th. But on this photograph we see people who had arrived with few of their possessions, and they were practically unloaded in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Just to be clear about when this photograph was taken, was this taken at the same time as the photograph that we saw on the previous photograph, page 44, or was this at a different time?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. A couple of minutes before or later.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Moving on to page 47.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: This is one of the photographs taken on the 28th of August. On this one we see an elderly woman with some of her possessions in her hands, and we also see a canister of the kind distributed by the Spanish Battalion of the UNPROFOR. They also distributed them to children. In fact, they distributed such canisters to children, so I suppose this woman had arrived in the company of a child.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Through the interpretation I was hearing the word "canister." I'm not completely sure what your mean when you refer to canister. At least that's how it's coming through in the English translation. Perhaps it is a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Jerrycan? Would that be more understandable?

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: We're referring to what you see looks like a balloon [Realtime transcript read in error "battalion"] under the right arm of the witness. Could it be a balloon?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's apology. It's the same word for balloon and jerrycan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is a balloon; it is not a canister.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the photograph at page 48.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph we see again the fence of the hydro power plant at Grabovica. In the background on the hill, which is on the other side of the Neretva River, we see fires. Those fires, as I was told then on the spot by the guard who was there at the hydro power plant, resulted from fire being opened from HVO positions against ABH positions at Dreznica. And the incendiary bullets that did not hit ABH but flew across ended up there and caused fire. And those combat activities happened looking from this position down the Neretva to the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Moving on to page 49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little detail. On this photo there seem to be two children with two balloons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They are inflating them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Moving on, photograph 49 -- page 49, please.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph we see an exhausted man. In fact, a group of people who are exhausted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] There it is. You say about this fire. How far were the hills with HVO positions from Grabovica? How many kilometres is it from the hill to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You could have asked that during your cross-examination. Mr. Karnavas agrees. So continue, Ms. Gillett. You will come back to that during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know what's happening to microphones, this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm trying.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: My pearls of wisdom, you can do without them for the moment perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Moving to page 50, please. And -- page 50, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this photograph we see UNPROFOR soldiers helping a woman off the truck, and I believe that we can see on this photograph that the woman is wearing traditional Muslim clothes, a multicoloured scarf --

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: On --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: -- which is not typical of other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: On to page 51, please. Page 55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, when we see this photo of a smiling boy, I in fact noticed several photographs of that kind, including the next one. What was your impression when you saw those civilians there? Did they look frightened, or did they look happy to be there? What was the feeling they exude? Because if we look at this photograph, we don't have the impression that they were victims of a great misfortune. I'm talking of course only about the women and children, not those who had been released from a prison. What was your feeling when you saw those images? And the same could be said of the photograph that follows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can briefly comment on that. All the people who had arrived, the women and the children, the grown-ups were happy that they had finally reach the territory controlled by the ABH, because they were sure that the maltreatment that they had been subjected to while in their homes is now over. They felt safer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honours, since Mr. Stewart's microphone was not working but he was able to tell me his concern, Your Honour, it is a matter which perhaps the transcript should be clarified. Back on page 97, there was a very strange translation which came out in English as battalion, which clearly was not the right word. I think it was the translation of the word which originally had been translated as a canister and it caused some confusion, and particularly in lines 23 and 24 on page 97 there's a strange sentence in the English translation, what looks like a battalion under the right arm of the witness. Clearly the reference was to a canister under the right arm of the woman. So perhaps that will help in clarifying the appropriate word there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did we not -- not -- were we not told instead of canister the word balloon should be used.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour, is it I think simply a typographical error in the transcript, it seems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I think a jerrycan might be suggested at one point, but clearly that might be something a little different. But I think Your Honour's quite right. But it came out as "battalion," which caused a certain confusion when it was translated back again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Passing on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's almost 7.00 p.m., everybody is tired. So let us hold on for another 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour, unless the Bench have any particular questions, I'm going to skip ahead -- skip some of the photographs so we don't have to go through the rest of the bundle in its entirety if the Chamber is in agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's the photograph you meant to produced, it's the person who is wearing his underwear. I believe that's 49. I think two photographs after the one we are looking at now.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Yes. That comes at page 62 of this exhibit bundle. If Your Honour has a question, it can certainly be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Sir, did you ask this person to take his trousers off? It was meant to show what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked this group of people who were standing at the entrance to the tunnel that one of them undress so that I could show in which condition they arrived at this location. They were embarrassed. They were embarrassed to be photographed. Some of them openly protested, while this young man thought differently. He volunteered. He said, "You can photograph me. I'm not afraid of anything," and he started taking his clothes off. This is the moment when he had taken his trousers off. He remained in his underwear, and he started taking off his -- the little chain he had around the neck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Gillett, will you now try to conclude your examination-in-chief within the remaining eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. Perhaps if the witness can be shown pages 103, 104, 105, 106, and 107. They can be shown one after the other, and I will ask the witness afterwards if he is able to provide information on them. It's not a problem if they're seen as a series.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, Witness, having seen those photographs, when were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: These photographs were not taken on the 28th. They were taken several days later when -- in fact, they were taken in the area of Grabovica, too, but not at the dam of the hydro power station but a couple of kilometres down in the barracks that had been used for the personnel of the hydro power station earlier. I returned after the prisoners were released with Maggie O'Kane, the reporter from the guardian whom I was assisting as an interpreter, and the agreement, the understanding was that I would take some photographs to a company for a story, and they were supposed to be send those photographs to London, unsuccessfully, as I told you before. But these photographs show the people who had been released from those prisons, but they were taken several days after their release.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, as to the remaining photographs both in this bundle and amongst the 110 photographs that you looked at earlier today, are there any other photographs of those remaining that we haven't seen that were not taken on the 28th of August or are all those remaining from the date of the 28th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN MALOVIC
utterances.text: I think all these photographs were taken on the 28th of August except for those that I indicated were taken at a different date.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions in examination-in-chief for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Regarding -- regarding the very last picture in this series of a man with a whitish beard sitting and one eye is bandaged, do you have information about the reasons of the injury that prompted the bandage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really cannot say. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your testimony will continue tomorrow, Witness. The Defence has one hour, and we are starting at 2.15 p.m. I believe the Bench has already asked most of their questions, and we will have little to add tomorrow, although I don't know for sure. In any case, your testimony will be over before the first break, I hope, and then we are going to continue with another witness. You are not going to meet any more with representatives of the OTP because you have already taken the solemn declaration, and you may not have contact with anyone at this point. I wish you a pleasant evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of February, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
